articles.title: Shag: Shag Avocado
articles.summary: Deep avocado green shag pile, dense mottled fuzz, satin sheen, reads as thick 70s carpet. Reads as a deep olive-avocado green with a lighter lime fuzz, like mossy felt; no shine at all.
articles.what: Two inches of pile in a colour named after a fruit, and a rake to comb it. Up close: A tangle of thin curling fibres in pale lime-yellow over a dark olive-green shadow, criss-crossing in every direction like long shag carpet pile or fine wire wool. Strands are hair-thin and very dense; dark gaps show between them. From a distance: Reads as a deep olive-avocado green with a lighter lime fuzz, like mossy felt; no shine at all. Measured spec (average): metal 2, roughness 100, coat 91. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.

how: Click the zone you want to change.

Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Doors, hood, roof: broad panels show the fibre tangle
Interior-themed accents or stripes in a pale colour
Cream, white or orange numbers read; green and brown numbers vanish into the pile.
Bold stripes and big blocks: the fibres are fine so solid graphics stay legible
Pairs well with: harvest gold, cream, brown, orange.
pitfalls: Not grass or moss with blades: strands are thin curly wires, no blade shapes
Not a velvet or suede smooth nap: the fibres are individually visible
Avoid: dark numbers on dark green, next to other fuzzy textures.

articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: dark numbers on dark green, next to other fuzzy textures.
